title: Simplicial latching colimits identify naturally with degenerate subsets
statement: Let $T:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ be a small simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and $n\geq0$. Let $\mathcal L_n$ have as objects the surjective order-preserving maps $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ with $k<n$. A morphism from $\sigma$ to $\sigma'$ is a surjection $\rho:[k']\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ satisfying $\sigma=\rho\sigma'$. Form the diagram $\sigma\mapsto T_k$, $\rho\mapsto T(\rho):T_k\to T_{k'}$, and its colimit $L_nT$ in sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The canonical map $\lambda_n:L_nT\to T_n$ induced by the $T(\sigma)$ is injective with image exactly $D_nT$, the set of degenerate $n$-simplices. Thus $L_nT\cong D_nT$, with the colimit structure map at $\sigma$ given by $T(\sigma)$ valued in $D_nT$. These identifications are natural under all maps of simplicial sets $T\to T'$, where $D_nT\to D_nT'$ is their restriction to the degenerate subsets. When $n=0$, both $L_0T$ and $D_0T$ are empty.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, statement and proof; consequence for the proper-surjection colimit. This colimit identification is the auxiliary latching calculation in Joyal–Tierney Section 2, Theorem 2.6 and Proposition 2.10, expanded by the agent rather than asserted as the literal statement of 017R.
